title: "Comparing Accelerated Failure Time Models"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(flexsurv)
library(eha)
library(survival)
```

# Parametric model

The accelerated failure time models compared include:

1.  Generalized F-model

2.  Generalized Gamma-model

3.  Log-logistic model

4.  Log-normal model

5.  Weibull model

6.  Exponential model

$Note:$ `aftreg` shows reversed sign in the coefficient estimates compared to other R functions since results used to prepare these comparison tables were generated from its default parameterization. This is discussed in R file. SE imply standard errors.

+-------------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Model             | Supported by R functions | Supported by SAS procedure | Match                                                                                         | Notes                                                                                                              |
+===================+==========================+============================+===============================================================================================+====================================================================================================================+
| Generalized F     | Yes                      | No                         | Comparison can only be made based on `Parmsurv SAS macro` as detailed in the comparison table | SAS `PROC LIFEREG` does not support Generalized F distribution model                                               |
+-------------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Generalized Gamma | Yes                      | Yes                        | similar results                                                                               | Can be formed in R using `flexsurvreg` but perfomed in SAS using `PROC LIFEREG` procedure and `Parmsurv SAS macro` |
+-------------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Log-Logistic      | Yes                      | Yes                        | similar results                                                                               | Can be performed with three R functions, `PROC LIFEREG` procedure and the `Parmsurv SAS macro`                     |
+-------------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Log-normal        | Yes                      | Yes                        | similar results                                                                               | Can be performed with three R functions, `PROC LIFEREG` procedure and the `Parmsurv SAS macro`                     |
+-------------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Weibull           | Yes                      | Yes                        | similar results                                                                               | Can be performed with three R functions, `PROC LIFEREG` procedure and the `Parmsurv SAS macro`                     |
+-------------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Exponential       | Yes                      | Yes                        | similar results                                                                               | Can be performed with three R functions, `PROC LIFEREG` procedure and the `Parmsurv SAS macro`                     |
+-------------------+--------------------------+----------------------------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

# Summary and Recommendation.

`flexsurvreg` is recommended mostly because of the flexibility it offers, and given that by modeling for generalized gamma and F, it includes models of interest as sub-models and performs some formal tests, which allows us to assess whether the sub-models would be suitable for the description of the data or not. `aftreg` uses a different parameterization which differs from standard AFT models in `survreg` and `flexsurvreg`, thus generating reversed regression coefficients. The default parameterization is `lifeAcc`. Using `lifeExp` ensures that the regression coefficients are consistent with those generated by the `flexsurvreg` and `survreg` functions. Just like `survreg`, it offers a limited set of distributions. There is a need to investigate the inverted sign estimates under `flexsurvreg` for the exponential model which makes the estimates identical to `aftreg` estimates. The `Parmsurv SAS macro` generates results which are consistent with results from `PROC LIFEREG`. There are minor differences in the least significant decimal places, and these do not seem to greatly affect the general exponential interpretation of results. The AIC and BIC are consistent across the models.
